findings: No injection surface: the section markup interpolates only static FACTS values. No request input reaches the HTML or the served JS. The /take-apart?from=home link is fixed and same-origin.

The new routes /home-layers.js and /img/home-layers.webp serve build-time constants with explicit content types through the existing text() and webp() helpers. They take no parameters, so there is no traversal or reflection.

The client module has no innerHTML, eval or document.write. It sets only dataset and aria attributes from numeric and index values. All imports are same-origin: the existing vendored routes, /models/patch-one.glb and /take-apart-model.js. There are no third-party origins and no new vendored copies.

The lazy gate and the mount function fail safe. The dynamic import has a catch, and mount has a try/catch that disposes the renderer. On failure the static fallback image and the HTML layer list remain.

Non-blocking: the repo sets no CSP or nosniff headers on any route. The inline module script and inline import map would need hashes or unsafe-inline if a CSP is added later. This was already the case before this change. The new routes set no cache-control header. The GLB keeps its existing 24 h cache header.
